roadmap.goal: Three copy-and-hint Stories, each its own slice that ships and closes alone, frontend only (no endpoint, payload, persistence or tracker call changes). Slice 01 (#6348): the always-visible helper line under Closed Items Cutoff (days) says what the number limits, in the owner's configured term (Work Items on a Team, Features on a Portfolio), with no info icon (MD-1). Slice 02 (#6352): an info button named 'About {field label}' beside Parent Override Field and Dependency Field wherever they are chosen (Team settings, Portfolio settings, the connection's defaults) opens the dashboard widgets' popover, extracted as a shared InfoPopoverButton (MD-5, DDD-1), with tracker-aware direction copy from one module and a Learn More link to the matching docs section in a new tab. Slice 03 (#6355): the Release picker invites searching ('Type to search Jira Releases') and a dateless Release reads 'No date in {tracker}: set one there to follow it' (MD-3, DDD-6). Done when every pending scenario in the DISTILL Scenarios table is un-skipped and green, every active guard stays green, no `it.skip` remains in the seven DISTILL test files, `__SCAFFOLD__` is gone from fieldDirectionTips.ts, and `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` (tsc + Biome) are clean with zero warnings. Docs (the Cut Off Days retitle and Team default 365, the Learn More target sections, the Following a Jira Release section), screenshots, release notes and StrykerJS on frozen code belong to finalization and are NOT steps here.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply, deliberately: the frontend is TypeScript + Vitest + React Testing Library and the project references no property-testing library. DISTILL authored every acceptance scenario, example-based, with the finite tracker axis as `it.skip.each`. RED is removing `it.skip` and watching the scenario fail on its assertion, as distill/red-classification.md records; GREEN is production code. Existing tests are edited only where DISTILL's Pre-requisites for DELIVER say so (the required-prop renders, the old Release caption, the second-review hardening items), in the same commit as the change that makes them necessary.
exit_gates: End of every step: the touched Vitest files green; `pnpm build` clean with zero warnings (prebuild runs `biome check --write`, so run `pnpm exec biome check ./src` read-only first and look at what it would rewrite).
End of every phase: the full `pnpm test` green and `pnpm build` clean; that phase's slice is releasable alone.

End of phase 02: run the existing Playwright spec that uses `BaseEditPage`'s 'Parent Override Field' combobox locally once; the info button sits beside the combobox and must not change its accessible name.

End of phase 03: the sibling `DeliverySourceTab.*` suites mock the terminology hook and answer the key for an unmapped term; read their output once the tab reads the work-tracking-system term and confirm nothing reads oddly.
Comments in new code: rare, plain-language why, never an internal reference (no MD-, D-, DDD-, AC- or ADR- numbers).
Every user-visible word a tenant can rename comes from the terminology hook; defaults follow TerminologySeeder (Work Items, Features), never Epic or Story.

MD-3 - #6355 inline caption 'No date in {tracker}: set one there to follow it'; placeholder 'Type to search {source name}s' ('Type to search Jira Releases'); 'No longer available' unchanged.

A source the tab cannot name a tracker for reads 'Type to search {source name}s' and 'No date in {tenant's work tracking system term}: set one there to follow it' (e.g. 'Tracker').
A retired Release still reads 'No longer available', never the missing-date advice, and stays unpickable.

While the options load the spinner shows as today and on a failed load the existing could-not-load message shows; the loading look (spinner in place of the picker) and the failure look (the could-not-load alert) are unchanged, as the two picker guards pin.
Touched Vitest files green; `pnpm build` clean (tsc + Biome); no comment cites an internal reference; configurable terms throughout.
